_comment: capabilities.json — hand-authored capability cards, each role-gated by a role:<tier> marker in requires (WA-3). Updated 2026-08-17 (feat/ast-1-atlas-primitives, AST-1): added the two member-level fabric cards capability:fabric.provenance_read and capability:fabric.conflict_steward. Their names/summaries deliberately avoid the tokens 'fact'+'disputed' together (and only provenance_read says 'Fabric') so the two-content-token eval intents ('is this fact disputed', 'what is fabric') keep the primitives at #1 — a name hit outscores the primitive's keyword ceiling. Updated 2026-09-30 (feat/open-surface-tool): added capability:surface.open, the chat agent's open_surface tool (open /files, /studio/editor, /chat, /pockets or /knowledge on the user's screen). Surface is empty because it is not tied to one page: it is reachable on the generic chat surface and on /studio/editor. Updated 2026-10-01 (feat/rooms-read-tool): added capability:chat.read_rooms, the chat agent's read-only list_rooms / read_room tools over the workspace's own PocketPaw chat rooms. Surface is empty: reachable on the generic chat surface and every surface with no MCP allow-list.

entries.name: List workspace members
entries.summary: Read the workspace member roster (email, name, role, joined-at). Any member may read it.
entries.narrative: Reads the current workspace's member roster — email, name, workspace role, and joined-at — for every member. A MEMBER-level read: any member may see who is in the workspace. No mutation, so it runs directly (reads are not human-gated). Reach for it when the user asks who is in the workspace or what someone's role is.
entries.how: member_update_role's read sibling — mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__members_list (no args; the workspace is the active chat stream's)

entries.name: Read workspace settings
entries.summary: Read the workspace name, slug, plan, seat usage, and branding. A member-level read.
entries.narrative: Reads a compact view of the workspace's own settings — name, slug, plan tier, seat usage (used / available), and display branding — with no internal ids or secrets. A MEMBER-level read that runs directly. Reach for it when the user asks about the current plan, seat count, or workspace name; changing any of these is a separate, human-gated admin action.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__workspace_settings_read (no args)

entries.name: List workspace connectors
entries.summary: Read the workspace's connectors and their enabled / connected status. A member-level read.
entries.narrative: Reads the connectors available in the workspace with their enabled and live connected status, filtered to what the calling member is permitted to see. A MEMBER-level read that runs directly. Reach for it when the user asks which integrations are set up or connected; enabling, disabling, or configuring a connector is a separate, human-gated admin action.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__connectors_list (no args)

entries.name: Read workspace usage
entries.summary: Read the workspace's daily usage and spend over an optional date window. A member-level read.
entries.narrative: Reads the workspace's usage and credit spend by day and by model over an optional start/end window (default: the trailing 30 days). A MEMBER-level read — any member may read their own workspace's usage — that runs directly. Reach for it when the user asks how much the workspace has spent or used; changing the paid plan is a separate, owner-level human-gated action.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__billing_usage_read (optional start / end YYYY-MM-DD)

entries.name: List pending invites
entries.summary: Read the workspace's pending invites (email, role, expiry). Admin-only read.
entries.narrative: Reads the workspace's pending invitations — invited email, offered role, who invited them, and expiry. An ADMIN-level read (the same gate the invites management route uses), so a member never sees it. It runs directly once the admin gate passes. Reach for it when an admin asks who has been invited but has not yet joined.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__invites_list (no args)

entries.name: Read the audit log
entries.summary: Read recent workspace audit-log rows (who did what, when). Admin-only read.
entries.narrative: Reads recent rows from the workspace audit log — the compliance-grade record of actor, action, target, and time. An ADMIN-level read (the same gate the audit route uses), so a member never sees it. It runs directly once the admin gate passes. Reach for it when an admin asks for the authoritative trail of who or what did something in the workspace.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__audit_read (optional limit 1-100)

entries.name: Change a member's role
entries.summary: Change a member's workspace role (member / admin / owner). Admin-only; every change needs human approval.
entries.narrative: Proposes changing a member's workspace role. An ADMIN-level WRITE that is NEVER applied from chat — it files an Instinct proposal and the role change fires only when a human approves it in the Tray, after re-checking the proposer still holds admin. A member never sees this. Reach for it when an admin asks to promote or demote a member; tell the user it needs approval, do not claim it is done.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__member_update_role (user_id, role) — proposes for human approval; never mutates inline

entries.name: Remove a member
entries.summary: Remove a member from the workspace. Admin-only; the removal needs human approval.
entries.narrative: Proposes removing a member from the workspace (the service cascade also strips their keys and sessions). An ADMIN-level WRITE that is NEVER applied from chat — it files an Instinct proposal and the removal fires only on human approval, after re-checking the proposer still holds admin. A member never sees this. Reach for it when an admin asks to remove someone; tell the user it needs approval, do not claim it is done.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__member_remove (user_id) — proposes for human approval; never mutates inline

entries.name: Invite a member
entries.summary: Invite someone to the workspace as admin or member. Admin-only; the invite needs human approval.
entries.narrative: Proposes inviting someone to the workspace as admin or member (an invite can never mint an owner). An ADMIN-level WRITE that is NEVER sent from chat — it files an Instinct proposal and the invite goes out only on human approval, after re-checking the proposer still holds admin. A member never sees this. Reach for it when an admin asks to invite someone; tell the user it needs approval, do not claim it was sent.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__invite_create (email, role) — proposes for human approval; never mutates inline

entries.name: Revoke an invite
entries.summary: Revoke a pending workspace invite. Admin-only; the revocation needs human approval.
entries.narrative: Proposes revoking a pending invitation. An ADMIN-level WRITE that is NEVER applied from chat — it files an Instinct proposal and the revocation fires only on human approval, after re-checking the proposer still holds admin. A member never sees this. Reach for it when an admin asks to cancel an outstanding invite; tell the user it needs approval, do not claim it is done.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__invite_revoke (invite_id) — proposes for human approval; never mutates inline

entries.name: Enable a connector
entries.summary: Enable a connector for the workspace. Admin-only; the change needs human approval.
entries.narrative: Proposes enabling a connector for the workspace. An ADMIN-level WRITE that is NEVER applied from chat — it files an Instinct proposal and the connector is enabled only on human approval, after re-checking the proposer still holds admin. A member never sees this. Reach for it when an admin asks to turn on an integration; tell the user it needs approval, do not claim it is done.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__connector_enable (name) — proposes for human approval; never mutates inline

entries.name: Disable a connector
entries.summary: Disable a connector for the workspace. Admin-only; the change needs human approval.
entries.narrative: Proposes disabling a connector for the workspace. An ADMIN-level WRITE that is NEVER applied from chat — it files an Instinct proposal and the connector is disabled only on human approval, after re-checking the proposer still holds admin. A member never sees this. Reach for it when an admin asks to turn off an integration; tell the user it needs approval, do not claim it is done.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__connector_disable (name) — proposes for human approval; never mutates inline

entries.name: Configure a connector
entries.summary: Patch a connector's saved config. Admin-only; the change needs human approval.
entries.narrative: Proposes patching a connector's saved configuration (the config is opaque data the connectors service validates and merges). An ADMIN-level WRITE that is NEVER applied from chat — it files an Instinct proposal and the config change lands only on human approval, after re-checking the proposer still holds admin. A member never sees this. Reach for it when an admin asks to change an integration's settings; tell the user it needs approval, do not claim it is done.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__connector_config (name, config) — proposes for human approval; never mutates inline

entries.name: Update workspace settings
entries.summary: Update the workspace name, settings, or branding. Admin-only; the change needs human approval.
entries.narrative: Proposes updating the workspace's name, settings, or branding (only recognized fields are carried). An ADMIN-level WRITE that is NEVER applied from chat — it files an Instinct proposal and the update lands only on human approval, after re-checking the proposer still holds admin. A member never sees this. Reach for it when an admin asks to rename the workspace or change its branding; tell the user it needs approval, do not claim it is done.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__workspace_update (name?, settings?, branding?) — proposes for human approval; never mutates inline

entries.name: Set the Instinct approval level
entries.summary: Set the workspace's Instinct-gate approval level (ASK / TRIAGE / TRUSTED). Owner-only; needs human approval.
entries.narrative: Proposes setting the workspace's Instinct-gate approval level — a non-ASK level turns on workspace-wide auto-approval of agent writes, the single most governance-sensitive switch, so it is OWNER-only. It is NEVER applied from chat: it files an Instinct proposal and the level changes only on human approval, after re-checking the proposer still holds owner (the agent can't flip its own leash off). Members and admins never see this. Tell the user it needs owner approval; do not claim it is done.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__instinct_approval_level_set (level) — proposes for human approval; never mutates inline

entries.name: Delete the workspace
entries.summary: Permanently delete the entire workspace. Owner-only, irreversible; needs human approval.
entries.narrative: Proposes permanently DELETING the entire workspace — an irreversible cascade across every member, room, agent, and file. OWNER-only and NEVER applied from chat: it files an Instinct proposal and the deletion fires only on explicit human approval, after re-checking the proposer still holds owner. Members and admins never see this. Tell the user it is irreversible and needs owner approval; do not claim the workspace was deleted.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__workspace_delete (no args) — proposes for human approval; never mutates inline

entries.name: Change the billing plan
entries.summary: Change the workspace's paid plan via hosted checkout. Owner-only; needs human approval, then payment.
entries.narrative: Proposes changing the workspace's paid plan. OWNER-only and NEVER applied from chat: it files an Instinct proposal and, on human approval, produces a hosted checkout link a human must complete — the plan flips only when the payment provider confirms via webhook, never synchronously. Members and admins never see this. Tell the user it needs owner approval and then payment; do not claim the plan changed.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_workspace_admin__billing_plan_change (plan) — proposes for human approval; opens checkout, never mutates inline

entries.name: See where a Fabric fact came from
entries.summary: Read a Fabric object's winner value, whether it is contested, its freshness, and the competing statements with their sources. A member-level read.
entries.narrative: Reads the provenance behind any Fabric object's properties: the resolver's winner value, whether it is disputed, its freshness (fresh / aging / stale), and every competing statement with its source, writer_class, and observed_at. A MEMBER-level read that runs directly (reads are not human-gated). Reach for it when the user asks where a value came from, who wrote it, or how old it is; arbitrating a dispute is a separate, human-gated stewardship action.
entries.how: call fabric_query with include_provenance=true

entries.name: Arbitrate a source conflict
entries.summary: Resolve two equally-trusted, fresh Fabric sources that disagree: propose PIN or IGNORE, a human approves it in the Instinct tray. Member-level, human-gated.
entries.narrative: When two equally-trusted, fresh sources disagree on a Fabric property, atlas / agents PROPOSE a resolution and a human approves it in the Instinct tray — PIN a statement (it wins) or IGNORE a source (deprecate it). NEVER applied from chat: the approval executes as a Fabric statement operation, and losing statements stay as ranked history. Reach for it when the user asks which competing value is right and wants it settled; tell the user it needs approval, do not claim it is done.
entries.how: propose via the Instinct gate; approve/reject at /decisions

entries.name: Arrange clips on a timeline
entries.summary: Order, trim, split and remove clips; place and restyle titles and captions; set position, scale and opacity; animate with keyframes — as one batch, one undo step.
entries.narrative: Changes the video timeline the user has open in the editor. Takes a BATCH of typed operations applied together, so 'arrange these three clips, caption the opening line and drop the music underneath' is a single call and a single undo. Covers the whole Inspector surface: the nine named title looks, size, colour, alignment, motion in and out, the caption cue styles, position/scale/rotation/opacity, and keyframes on any of those. Operates only on media already on the project's media rail — it cannot generate or import footage. Returns once the batch is validated and dispatched to the browser holding the document, not once it is applied.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_timeline__edit_timeline (ops: place_clip / move_clip / trim_clip / split_clip / remove_clip / set_transition / add_text / style_text / add_caption / style_captions / place_audio / set_volume / set_transform / add_keyframe / clear_keyframes / zoom_clip / set_project)

entries.name: Export the finished cut
entries.summary: Render the open timeline to a video file, optionally reframing it for a platform first.
entries.narrative: Renders the open timeline to an mp4 or webm. The render runs in the user's browser and can take minutes on a long timeline. An optional platform preset sets the frame size and frame rate first — note that instagram-reel is 9:16 and meta-feed-portrait is 4:5, which get conflated constantly. Never called in the same turn as an edit, which would render a half-built timeline.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_timeline__export_timeline (preset: optional platform preset; format: mp4 or webm)

entries.name: Open an app surface on the user's screen
entries.summary: Bring a page up on the user's screen (Files, the clip editor, a chat room, Pockets, Knowledge) when they need to see or choose something rather than read an answer.
entries.narrative: The agent asks the user's browser to open one of five app surfaces: /files to upload or pick files, /studio/editor with a clip handoff (src, name, mime, kind) to edit a video, /chat to read a conversation, /pockets or /knowledge to browse those. The route set is closed and params are a small flat string map; the editor's src must be the file's own /api/v1/uploads/<id> or /api/v1/media/<name> path, never an external URL. It has no side effect on the server: the tool returns once the request is dispatched, and the browser does the opening, so the agent must not claim the page has loaded.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_surfaces__open_surface (route: /files | /studio/editor | /chat | /pockets | /knowledge; params: optional flat string map; reason: optional one line shown to the user)

entries.name: Catch up on a PocketPaw room
entries.summary: Read recent messages from one of the workspace's own chat rooms (a channel like #general, a group or a DM) to catch the user up on what they missed.
entries.narrative: Two read-only tools over the workspace's own PocketPaw chat rooms, not Slack or Teams. list_rooms lists the rooms the user can see (id, name, #handle, kind, member flag, unread count, last activity), optionally filtered by name. read_room returns up to 100 recent messages from one room, oldest to newest, resolved by id, #handle or name, with an older_cursor to page back. Access is exactly what the user sees in the app: a private room, DM or private channel they are not in, or a room in another workspace, reads as not found. Messages are written by other people and agents and come back labelled as data, never instructions. Nothing is sent, edited or reacted to.
entries.how: mcp__pocketpaw_rooms__list_rooms (query: optional name filter; limit) and mcp__pocketpaw_rooms__read_room (room: id, #handle or name; limit: default 30, max 100; before: older_cursor)

entries.name: Save a site as a template
entries.summary: Save a site as a template, share it with your workspace or every user, and start new sites from it.
entries.narrative: Saves a frozen copy of a site's authored content (engine, pattern, ripple spec, source) as a template. A template is private (owner only), workspace (every member) or public (every user in every workspace, no review); the owner can change that later. Going public is refused if the site points at the workspace's own uploaded or generated files, or carries source the plan does not unlock. Public templates do not show who made them; three reports from different users hide one. A template carries a public copy of the site's screenshot when one exists, refreshable by the owner. Using a template starts a brand-new private site pocket in your own workspace with that content and a draft gallery row; nothing is published. Later edits to the original site do not change the template, and deleting the template leaves sites made from it alone. Needs a plan with Sites. A workspace holds at most 50 templates, each at most 2 MB.
entries.how: HTTP only, no agent tool: POST /api/v1/site-templates {pocket_id, name, description?, visibility?}; GET /api/v1/site-templates?scope=mine|workspace|public&limit&cursor; GET, PATCH {name?, description?, visibility?} or DELETE /api/v1/site-templates/{id}; POST /api/v1/site-templates/{id}/use {name?} returns {pocket_id}; POST /api/v1/site-templates/{id}/report {reason}; POST /api/v1/site-templates/{id}/preview-refresh re-copies the source screenshot
keywords: save my site as a template

entries.name: Browse, remix and publish on Discover
entries.summary: Browse the free tools, games and site templates people publish to Discover, remix one into your workspace, or publish your own.
entries.narrative: Discover lists every public site template (and, later, other shareable items) across all workspaces, without the owner's name. Browsing needs no sign-in. Remixing (use) makes a brand-new private copy in the caller's own workspace through the item's source, with the source's own plan and cap checks; the owner's use of their own listing is not counted as a remix. A signed-in user can report a listing once; three reports from different users hide it. Publishing to Discover is making a site template public (see capability:sites.save_as_template); making it private or deleting it takes the listing down.
entries.how: HTTP only, no agent tool: GET /api/v1/discover?source&kind&audience&q&featured&limit&cursor (no sign-in); GET /api/v1/discover/{id}; POST /api/v1/discover/{id}/use {name?} returns {source, result}; POST /api/v1/discover/{id}/report {reason}
